deep.reconstruction:
This page opens section (1), 'topological cases', of a systematic catalogue of the Teichmüller groupoids. The previous page lists the 'twelve avatars' of the Teichmüller tower: topological, differentiable, C-analytic, hyperbolic, C-algebraic, Q̄-algebraic, combinatorial via maps, Lego and pants.

(i) The simplest variant is T^+_top = T_top, the 'oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid'.
- Objects: compact oriented surfaces with boundary S.
- Morphisms: isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms.
- Its automorphism groups are the orientation-preserving mapping class groups Mod^+(S). The boundary convention (whether isotopies fix the boundary pointwise) is not specified here.

(ii) The 'immediate variant' is T^±_top, the 'bi-oriented' groupoid. It has the same objects, and its arrows are isotopy classes of all homeomorphisms, not necessarily orientation-preserving. Its automorphism groups are the extended mapping class groups Mod^±(S).

(iii) Let [±1] be the one-object groupoid (object e, e.g. e = ∅) with automorphism group {±1}. There is a 'signature' functor χ: T^±_top → [±1], sending a homeomorphism to +1 or −1 according to whether it preserves orientation. Its fibre (kernel) is T^+_top. This is the groupoid form of the exact sequence 1 → Mod^+(S) → Mod^±(S) → {±1}.

(iv) The left-margin note reads: 'connexité, si on se borne à des surfaces connexes !' It flags that χ is only well defined for connected surfaces. On a disconnected surface a homeomorphism can preserve orientation on some components and reverse it on others, so the natural invariant lies in a product of ±1's over the components, not in ±1.

(v) The 'most complex' variant is announced as S_*TD^+_top: the 'special decorated (oriented) topological Teichmüller groupoid'. Decorations are presumably boundary parametrizations and/or marked points with tangent data, cf. Π'_diff on the previous page. The right-margin note is mostly illegible. It seems to say that one should fix once and for all an oriented reference circle S^1, presumably so that boundary parametrizations become decorations comparable across surfaces, and it refers to some T^±- or C^*-type objects.

Purpose: to set up, uniformly across the avatars, the categorical objects (groupoids of surfaces and mapping classes) whose comparison is the 'Teichmüller tower' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: The signature morphism χ: T^±_top → [±1] is not well defined if disconnected surfaces are allowed as objects. Grothendieck himself flags this in the left margin ('si on se borne à des surfaces connexes'). For disconnected S the correct target is a product of ±1 over π0(S), or a wreath-type extension.

If e = ∅ is meant as the empty surface, its automorphism group in T^±_top is trivial, not ±1. So the example e = ∅ is merely a label for the abstract one-object groupoid, not an object of T^±_top. This is harmless, but the notation could mislead.

The boundary behaviour of isotopies (fixed pointwise or free) is not specified. This changes the groupoid: for a surface with boundary, the mapping class group rel boundary is a central extension by Dehn twists along the boundary. Presumably the 'decorated' variants are meant to address this.

ideas.what: Groupoid whose objects are compact oriented surfaces with boundary and whose arrows are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms (the Teichmüller groupoid, topological avatar)
ideas.modern_name: mapping class groupoid / Teichmüller groupoid (topological model)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); formalized later by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Funar and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Extended (orientation-not-necessarily-preserved) variant T^± with signature functor to [±1] whose kernel is T^+
ideas.modern_name: extended mapping class group(oid), exact sequence 1→Mod^+→Mod^±→Z/2

ideas.what: Remark that the orientation character only exists for connected surfaces
Announcement of a 'special decorated' oriented topological Teichmüller groupoid S_*TD^+_top, apparently with a fixed reference oriented circle for boundary data
ideas.modern_name: groupoid of surfaces with parametrized boundaries / decorated mapping class groupoid (as in Lego–Teichmüller game, modular functors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego–Teichmüller game, ~2000), Segal-type bordism categories
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions Lego and decorated surfaces only in outline

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard definitions of the mapping class groupoid and its orientation-extended version, with a correct self-caveat about connectedness. The 'special decorated' variant is only named on this page, not developed. It is in the spirit of what Bakalov–Kirillov and others later formalized, so nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Left margin: read 'connexité, si on se borne à des surfaces connexes !' rather than 'si on veut des bouts à des surfaces connexes'. The note is a caveat that the signature χ requires connected surfaces.
Line under S_*TD: the word 'orienté' is written above as an insertion, giving 'groupoïde de Teichmüller orienté spécial décoré topologique'.

Right margin: most of the transcription is unreliable. The legible parts suggest it begins 'Fixant une fois pour toutes un [cercle?] orienté (S^1 par exemple)…'. The symbol read as 'C^±' is more likely T^± (a Teichmüller groupoid), and 'C^*' may be 'T^*' or 'orientés'.
